decks.domain: Speed, traffic lights, signs, rail crossings and work zones

cards.front: What is the rule for rules of the road?
cards.back: Road travel is governed by traffic signs, signals, pavement markings and driving laws that every driver must obey.

cards.front: What is the rule for speed increases danger?
cards.back: Higher speed increases crash severity, reduces the ability to see or stop quickly and increases the chance of losing control.

cards.front: What is the rule for speed and reaction distance?
cards.back: At higher speed a vehicle covers more ground during reaction time and needs more distance to stop.

cards.front: What is the rule for speeding costs?
cards.back: Higher-speed driving uses more fuel and can bring fines and increased insurance costs.

cards.front: What is the rule for safe speed for conditions?
cards.back: The fundamental speed rule prohibits traveling faster than is safe for traffic, road surface, weather, visibility and nearby unprotected road users.

cards.front: What is the rule for limit is not a target?
cards.back: Poor conditions or hazards require a lower speed even when the posted limit is higher.

cards.front: What is the rule for posted maximum?
cards.back: Never exceed a posted speed limit, which assumes ideal conditions.

cards.front: What is the rule for source highway limit range?
cards.back: The manual describes limited-access highway speed limits from fifty to sixty-five miles per hour and smaller-highway limits of fifty-five or less.

cards.front: What is the rule for Turnpike minimum?
cards.back: The Massachusetts Turnpike has a forty-mile-per-hour minimum speed.

cards.front: What is the rule for Harbor tunnel minimum?
cards.back: The Callahan, Sumner and Ted Williams tunnels have a twenty-mile-per-hour minimum speed.

cards.front: What is the rule for unreasonably slow traffic?
cards.back: An officer may direct a driver who is delaying traffic to the side of a state highway even without a posted minimum speed.

cards.front: What is the rule for school zone default?
cards.back: Unless another limit is posted, speed above twenty miles per hour in a school zone is not reasonable and proper.

cards.front: What is the rule for settled district threshold?
cards.back: The default reasonable-and-proper threshold in a thickly settled or business district is thirty miles per hour unless signs establish twenty-five.

cards.front: What is the rule for outside district thresholds?
cards.back: Outside a thickly settled or business district, the stated default threshold is forty miles per hour, or fifty on a highway, unless posted otherwise.

cards.front: What is the rule for thickly settled definition?
cards.back: A thickly settled district has buildings less than two hundred feet apart for at least a quarter of a mile.

cards.front: What is the rule for municipal settled limit?
cards.back: Some municipalities establish a twenty-five-mile-per-hour thickly settled limit unless otherwise posted and mark the city or town entrances.

cards.front: What is the rule for school zone sign conditions?
cards.back: The school-zone limit is twenty miles per hour and may be indicated by flashing yellow lights or signs applying during specified hours.

cards.front: What is the rule for school zone vigilance?
cards.back: In a school zone, watch for children walking or bicycling and for school patrols or crossing guards.

decks.domain: Speed, traffic lights, signs, rail crossings and work zones

cards.front: What is the rule for signal order?
cards.back: The usual round traffic-signal lights are red at the top, yellow in the middle and green at the bottom.

cards.front: What is the rule for steady red?
cards.back: A steady red round signal requires a complete stop until green except for a permitted turn on red.

cards.front: What is the rule for right on red conditions?
cards.back: A right turn on red is allowed only after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and other traffic, and is forbidden when a No Turn on Red sign is posted.

cards.front: What is the rule for one way left on red?
cards.back: A left turn on red is allowed from a one-way street onto another one-way street after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

cards.front: What is the rule for Massachusetts red arrow?
cards.back: In Massachusetts a steady red arrow applies the round-red rules to vehicles traveling in its direction, including the same permitted-turn-on-red rules.

cards.front: What is the rule for flashing red?
cards.back: A flashing red signal requires the same complete stop and safe yielding as a stop sign.

cards.front: What is the rule for flashing red stop position?
cards.back: At flashing red, stop before a marked stop line or crosswalk; without a line, stop where you can see traffic before entering the intersection.

cards.front: What is the rule for steady yellow?
cards.back: A steady yellow signal announces the change from green to red and requires stopping when safe.

cards.front: What is the rule for no yellow start?
cards.back: A driver already stopped at an intersection or stop line must not start through on steady yellow.

cards.front: What is the rule for flashing yellow?
cards.back: A flashing yellow signal calls for caution, alertness and checking both directions at an intersection.

cards.front: What is the rule for flashing arrow gap?
cards.back: A flashing yellow arrow permits a turn in its direction only after the driver finds a sufficient oncoming-traffic gap and a clear pedestrian path.

cards.front: What is the rule for green still requires yielding?
cards.back: Before proceeding on green, yield to vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians already in the road.

cards.front: What is the rule for do not block intersection?
cards.back: Enter an intersection on green only when there is room to get completely through without blocking it.

cards.front: What is the rule for left on green?
cards.back: A driver turning left on a steady green signal must yield to oncoming traffic.

cards.front: What is the rule for protected green arrow?
cards.back: A green arrow permits a protected turn in the arrow’s direction, with pedestrians and opposing traffic expected to face red.

cards.front: What is the rule for rapid flashing beacon?
cards.back: A pedestrian or detection system activates a rectangular rapid-flashing beacon, whose irregular amber flashes require drivers to stop for pedestrians.

cards.front: What is the rule for dark hybrid beacon?
cards.back: At an inactive pedestrian hybrid beacon with all lights dark, proceed cautiously.

cards.front: What is the rule for hybrid yellow sequence?
cards.back: A flashing yellow pedestrian-hybrid light requires slowing, and a steady yellow requires preparing to stop.

cards.front: What is the rule for hybrid steady red?
cards.back: Two steady red pedestrian-hybrid lights require a stop for pedestrians.

cards.front: What is the rule for hybrid flashing red?
cards.back: Two flashing red pedestrian-hybrid lights require a stop followed by cautious movement only if clear.

cards.front: What is the rule for bicycle specific signal?
cards.back: Bicycle signals use red, yellow and green bicycle symbols, allowing bicycle movement on green while motor traffic is stopped.

cards.front: What is the rule for flashing malfunction?
cards.back: A malfunctioning signal flashing red or yellow is obeyed according to the corresponding flashing-light rule.

cards.front: What is the rule for blacked out signal?
cards.back: A completely dark nonfunctioning traffic signal is treated cautiously as an all-way stop.

cards.front: What is the rule for countdown does not remove right of way?
cards.back: A pedestrian already in a crosswalk retains right of way after the pedestrian countdown reaches zero.

cards.front: What is the rule for crosswalk yielding?
cards.back: Drivers must yield to pedestrians entering or using a crosswalk in the vehicle’s path.

cards.front: What is the rule for keep crosswalk clear?
cards.back: A vehicle must never block a crosswalk.

cards.front: What is the rule for red pedestrian yielding?
cards.back: A driver must yield to pedestrians when facing a red signal or a red-and-yellow signal.

cards.front: What is the rule for do not pass yielding vehicle?
cards.back: Never pass a vehicle stopped or slowing for a pedestrian.

cards.front: What is the rule for driveway pedestrian priority?
cards.back: Yield to pedestrians while turning into a driveway or parking lot.

cards.front: What is the rule for pedestrian crossing facility?
cards.back: Pedestrians must use an available crosswalk and request the WALK phase with the button where one exists.

cards.front: What is the rule for pedestrian phase rules?
cards.back: A pedestrian may start crossing on WALK but must not start on DON’T WALK; someone already crossing should finish.

cards.front: What is the rule for pedestrian observation?
cards.back: Before crossing, a pedestrian should stop at the curb, look both ways and watch especially for turning vehicles.

decks.domain: Speed, traffic lights, signs, rail crossings and work zones

cards.front: What is the rule for red and green signs?
cards.back: Red traffic signs indicate stopping or prohibition, while green indicates direction and permitted destinations.

cards.front: What is the rule for warning and regulation colors?
cards.back: Yellow indicates general warnings, and black with white indicates regulation.

cards.front: What is the rule for service and destination colors?
cards.back: Blue identifies motorist services or evacuation routes, and brown identifies recreational, historic or scenic destinations.

cards.front: What is the rule for orange work warning?
cards.back: Orange warns of construction or maintenance.

cards.front: What is the rule for fluorescent yellow green?
cards.back: Fluorescent yellow-green is used for school, bicycle, pedestrian and curve warnings.

cards.front: What is the rule for incident and toll colors?
cards.back: Fluorescent pink identifies incident-management signs, while purple identifies electronic-toll signs.

cards.front: What is the rule for motorist service cues?
cards.back: The illustrated service signs identify information, fuel, telephone, food, lodging, hospital services, picnic areas and accessible facilities.

cards.front: What is the rule for bicycle guide signs?
cards.back: Bicycle-route and Bay State Greenway signs guide bicycle travel.

cards.front: What is the rule for numbered route junction?
cards.back: Junction signs announce an upcoming numbered-route junction.

cards.front: What is the rule for guide distance units?
cards.back: Destination and highway-exit distance signs express the illustrated distances in miles.

cards.front: What is the rule for mile markers?
cards.back: Highway mile markers identify mile positions along the highway.

cards.front: What is the rule for parking and rest guides?
cards.back: Parking signs direct drivers to parking facilities and rest-area signs identify highway rest areas.

cards.front: What is the rule for electronic tolling guide?
cards.back: A sign marked electronic tolling only identifies an electronic-only toll facility.

cards.front: What is the rule for stop and yield shapes?
cards.back: An octagonal sign shape identifies Stop, while a downward-pointing triangle identifies Yield.

cards.front: What is the rule for pennant and pentagon?
cards.back: A sideways pennant identifies a No Passing Zone, while a pentagon identifies a school zone.

cards.front: What is the rule for diamond and circle?
cards.back: A diamond is the illustrated warning-sign shape, while a circle is the railroad-crossing-warning shape.

cards.front: What is the rule for rectangle and shield shapes?
cards.back: The shape guide depicts a horizontal rectangle for guide information, a vertical rectangle for regulation and a shield for interstate highways.

cards.front: What is the rule for regulatory messages?
cards.back: Regulatory signs have red or white backgrounds and convey traffic laws through words, pictures or both.

cards.front: What is the rule for prohibition symbol?
cards.back: A red circle with a diagonal slash indicates a prohibition.

cards.front: What is the rule for warning response?
cards.back: Yellow or fluorescent yellow-green warnings announce hazards or changes ahead and call for slowing and obeying the warning.

cards.front: What is the rule for green highway guidance?
cards.back: Green guide signs provide highway directions and interchange guidance.

cards.front: What is the rule for Massachusetts route marker?
cards.back: Massachusetts numbered-state-route signs are white rectangles with black numbers and borders.

cards.front: What is the rule for interstate route marker?
cards.back: Interstate route markers are shields colored blue, red and white.

decks.domain: Speed, traffic lights, signs, rail crossings and work zones

cards.front: Which Yield, turn, and road-user signs open the regulatory sign chart?
cards.back: The regulatory sign chart opens with Yield alongside turn and road-user prohibitions covering right turns, left turns, U-turns, trucks, pedestrians, and bicycles.

cards.front: What is the rule for prohibited turn arrows?
cards.back: A crossed-out right-turn arrow prohibits a right turn, and a crossed-out left-turn arrow prohibits a left turn.

cards.front: What is the rule for no U turn cue?
cards.back: A crossed-out U-shaped turn arrow prohibits a U-turn.

cards.front: What is the rule for prohibited user symbols?
cards.back: Crossed-out truck, pedestrian and bicycle symbols prohibit the represented road user.

cards.front: What is the rule for posted parking hours?
cards.back: A parking prohibition sign with specified hours bars parking during those posted hours.

cards.front: What is the rule for one way direction?
cards.back: A One Way sign permits traffic movement only in its arrow’s direction.

cards.front: What is the rule for no passing instruction?
cards.back: A Do Not Pass sign prohibits overtaking another vehicle.

cards.front: What is the rule for no red light turn?
cards.back: A No Turn on Red sign prohibits the indicated turn after stopping at a red signal.

cards.front: What is the rule for left turn only lane?
cards.back: The illustrated left-turn arrow marked Only requires traffic in that lane to turn left.

cards.front: What is the rule for keep right divider cue?
cards.back: The illustrated arrow bending to the right of a divider directs traffic to keep right of the upcoming median or lane divider.

decks.domain: Speed, traffic lights, signs, rail crossings and work zones

cards.front: What is the rule for school sign cues?
cards.back: The illustrated pair of schoolchildren identifies a school zone, while a crossing version identifies the school crossing.

cards.front: What is the rule for merge right warning?
cards.back: A warning showing traffic joining the main upward arrow from the right indicates a merge from the right.

cards.front: What is the rule for divided highway changes?
cards.back: A divided-highway-begins warning indicates a divided road ahead, while the corresponding ending warning indicates the divider ends.

cards.front: What is the rule for multiple curves?
cards.back: A winding-road warning indicates several curves ahead.

cards.front: What is the rule for turn versus curve cue?
cards.back: A sharp right-angle arrow warns of a right turn, while a curved right arrow warns of a right curve.

cards.front: What is the rule for playground warning?
cards.back: A playground warning alerts the driver to a nearby playground.

cards.front: What is the rule for crossroad warning?
cards.back: A plus-shaped intersection warning indicates a crossroad ahead.

cards.front: What is the rule for soft shoulder?
cards.back: A Soft Shoulder warning indicates hazardous soft dirt beside the paved roadway.

cards.front: Which pedestrian warning signs appear in the warning sign chart?
cards.back: The warning sign chart includes both pedestrian crossing signs and a pedestrian crossing ahead sign.

cards.front: What is the rule for upcoming traffic controls?
cards.back: A stop-symbol advance warning indicates a stop ahead, while a traffic-light-symbol warning indicates a signal ahead.

cards.front: What is the rule for two way traffic cue?
cards.back: A warning with opposing vertical arrows indicates two-way traffic.

cards.front: What is the rule for right side road?
cards.back: A right-side branch on the intersection warning indicates a road entering from the right.

cards.front: What is the rule for no passing zone?
cards.back: The illustrated no-passing-zone warning says the yellow line may not be crossed.

cards.front: What is the rule for right lane ends?
cards.back: A right-lane-ending warning indicates the right lane narrows away.

cards.front: What is the rule for wet road warning?
cards.back: A car with curving skid tracks warns that the road is slippery when wet.

cards.front: What is the rule for T junction warning?
cards.back: A T-shaped road warning indicates the road ends at a junction.

cards.front: What is the rule for height clearance?
cards.back: A height-clearance warning states the maximum vehicle height that can pass.

cards.front: What is the rule for circular intersection?
cards.back: A circular-intersection warning indicates a rotary or similar circular intersection ahead.

cards.front: What is the rule for either side traffic cue?
cards.back: The illustrated arrows passing on both sides of a central obstruction indicate traffic may flow on either side of the sign.

cards.front: What is the rule for deer crossing?
cards.back: A deer-symbol warning indicates a deer crossing area.

cards.front: What is the rule for advance railroad warning?
cards.back: A round railroad warning indicates a railroad crossing ahead.

cards.front: How does the warning sign chart list added-lane and merging-lane warnings?
cards.back: The warning sign chart shows an added lane warning sign separately from the sign for a lane merging from the right, which tells drivers to watch for other traffic.

decks.domain: Speed, traffic lights, signs, rail crossings and work zones

cards.front: What is the rule for complete stop position?
cards.back: A Stop sign requires every approaching vehicle to halt completely before any stop line or crosswalk.

cards.front: What is the rule for stop then yield?
cards.back: After a stop, yield to pedestrians and other vehicles and proceed carefully; merely slowing is insufficient.

cards.front: What is the rule for all way stop order?
cards.back: An All Way or Four Way plaque requires traffic from every approach to stop, with priority for the first vehicle at the intersection or four-way stop.

cards.front: What is the rule for yield action?
cards.back: A Yield sign requires slowing and allowing vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians to proceed first, with a complete stop when conditions require.

decks.domain: Speed, traffic lights, signs, rail crossings and work zones

cards.front: What is the rule for train approach caution?
cards.back: An advance railroad warning calls for slowing and preparing to stop, never speeding up to beat an approaching train.

cards.front: What is the rule for crossbuck and track count?
cards.back: A white crossbuck marks where tracks cross the road, and a plaque below gives the track count when there is more than one.

cards.front: What is the rule for railroad stopping distance?
cards.back: When railroad-crossing red lights flash, stop at least fifteen feet before the light post or gate.

cards.front: What is the rule for wait for both conditions?
cards.back: Remain stopped until the railroad gate rises and the red lights stop flashing.

cards.front: What is the rule for no gate bypass?
cards.back: Never bypass a lowered railroad gate or ignore flashing lights even when no train is visible.

decks.domain: Speed, traffic lights, signs, rail crossings and work zones

cards.front: What is the rule for work zone approach?
cards.back: Reduce speed on approaching a work zone and look for traffic, obstructions and roadside hazards.

cards.front: What is the rule for traffic control directions?
cards.back: Obey a police officer’s or civilian flagger’s work-zone instructions, and an officer’s directions override signs, signals and pavement markings.

cards.front: What is the rule for avoid work zone distraction?
cards.back: Keep attention on driving rather than activity inside the work area.

cards.front: What is the rule for work zone sign sequence?
cards.back: Warning or electronic-message signs mark a work zone’s beginning and later signs explain where work is occurring and how to proceed.

cards.front: What is the rule for channelizing devices?
cards.back: Drums, cones and tubular markers guide traffic away from closed shoulders or lanes and call for a careful merge into the adjacent open lane.

cards.front: What is the rule for closed lane barricade?
cards.back: Barricades commonly block access to a lane closed to traffic.

cards.front: What is the rule for follow detour guidance?
cards.back: Detour signs guide traffic around a closed road or direction of travel and back to the original route.

cards.front: What is the rule for arrow board guidance?
cards.back: Portable arrow boards on multilane roads indicate a closed shoulder or lane and the open direction for a safe merge.
